title: Modernize Python/JS/Go clients and remove legacy API params
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Summary: Update Redwood official SDKs (Python, JavaScript, Go) to modern dependency versions, remove deprecated API surface parameters introduced in legacy clients, and run performance regression tests. Background: Past years accumulated ad-hoc compatibility shims and long-unpinned dependencies causing build flakes and unexpected transitive CVEs. Scope: bump core HTTP/transport libs, unify JSON/parsing crates, remove legacy request fields (e.g., legacy_stream, old_response_wrapper, allow_legacy_params), simplify client constructors, and update compatibility layer where strictly required. Out of scope: revamping public method names, large surface redesigns for v2 client; those will be follow-ups. Goals: reduce install size and transitive vulnerabilities, eliminate confusing legacy params, restore CI stability, and validate throughput/latency parity with current runtime. Deliverables: updated packages for python/redwood, @redwood/sdk, and go.redwood; migration guide; deprecation notice and automated compatibility transforms in the JS client for two release cycles; benchmark report and e2e test matrix.
acceptance_criteria: All three language clients build cleanly on hermetic CI with pinned transitive deps
Deprecated API params removed from public surface or behind feature flags
No regression >5% p50 latency or 10% throughput on standard perf harness compared to baseline
Migration guide published in docs with code examples for common upgrade paths
Security scan (Snyk/GH Dependabot) shows resolved critical/high transitive issues introduced by older pins
All SDK unit/integration tests pass and nightly canary runs succeed for 3 consecutive days
tasks: Audit current dependency graph for python/js/go and produce specific bump candidates (Aisha)
Prepare a compatibility matrix listing allowed breaking changes and shims (Marco)
Implement JS client transport modernization: replace legacy adapter with fetch + stream-friendly wrapper (ENG-33108)
Pin and test Python dependencies, migrate requests -> httpx or upgrade requests to latest secure minor (ENG-33109)
Replace Go dep 'old-json' with 'encoding/json' + small adapter to preserve behavior (ENG-33110)
Remove deprecated params from public constructors, add deprecation warnings for one release (feature flag rollout)
Add automated codemod script for common JS usage patterns to ease migration (deliver in repo /tools/codemods)
Run perf harness against runtime-1.20 baseline and collect p50/p95 and throughput numbers
Create PRs per-language with clear CHANGELOG entries and release notes
Coordinate console and runtime teams for compatibility checks and canary routing
comments: 2026-02-20 - Aisha: Initial dependency audit attached. Found 12 transitive libs with known advisories across languages. Prioritized by exploitability and transitive depth.

2026-02-25 - Marco: Decided to opt for httpx in Python for async support in future features. Will keep sync wrappers for backwards compatibility. Open question: pin httpcore to 0.15.x or 0.16.x? Security team prefers 0.16.x.
2026-03-02 - Lina Chen (Security): Confirmed two medium CVEs in old-js-logger; recommend upgrade to @redwood/logger v3 which includes safe-stdout changes. Filing ENG-33111 to follow up.

2026-03-05 - Marco: Implemented prototype of JS codemod to rewrite legacy params; PR opened https://github.com/redwood-ai/js-sdk/pull/1123. Needs review: ensures stream semantics preserved for chunked responses.

2026-03-09 - Aisha: Perf run round 1: Python client p50 increased by 3.2% on small-batch workload when enabling httpx; identified cooldown in connection pooling config. Action: tune pool settings and re-run.

2026-03-11 - Reviewer (Olaf Berg): Requested clearer migration guide for Go users who rely on the older response wrapper; suggested adding example transforms and a small shim package for one release cycle.
2026-03-12 - Marco: Merged JS transport PR behind feature flag 'modern_transport'. Will enable canary for 5% of traffic in hosted tests directory next week.
notes: Trade-offs discussed: aggressive unpinning reduces dev friction but risks transient CI failures; chosen approach is staged bumps with canary job gating.
We will maintain tiny compatibility shims for the next two minor releases and remove them in clients-2026.06 unless significant customer pushback.
Operational plan: after merge, enable modern client behind feature flag and run traffic for 72h on internal canary tenants before ramping.
QA checklist: run e2e with large prompt lengths (>=2048 tokens), streaming endpoints, function call payloads, and embeddings pipeline to catch encoding regressions.
Security: schedule a follow-up with Security to re-run dependency scanners post-merge and before publishing packages to registries.
Doc owners: @docs-team to publish migration guide; assign PR to Aisha for final sign-off.
